original_record.question:
In the picture there is a square tile with two fourths of a circle. The radius of every fourth is half the side of the tile and its length equals $5 \mathrm{dm}$. We form a large square from 16 such tiles and try to get the longest unbroken curve consisting of the fourths. How long can this continuous curve be at most?
<image1>
original_record.subject: combinatorial geometry

inventory.objects: square tile and two opposite-corner quarter circles, radius half tile side

answer_verification.method: Enumerate all2^16 rotation pairings in4x4 tiling. Connect arcs at shared side midpoints; every connected path/cycle component has degree at most2. Largest connected component has22 arcs; each length5dm, so110dm.
